cc:Work.dc:title: Misc - Frame
cc:Work.dc:description:
Flat frame or trim made of up to four mitred bars
A flat frame around an opening: a picture frame, a window or door trim, a bezel. The frame is cut as separate bars that lie in one plane. Neighbouring bars meet in a mitre and can be locked together with dove tails.
Each bar has its own width. Set the width of a bar to 0 to leave that side open:
* `bottom = 0` gives a 3-sided trim, e.g. a window casing above a sill * `bottom = 0` and `right = 0` gives an L shape
Where both bars of a corner have the same width the mitre is 45°. With different widths the mitre runs from the inner corner to the outer corner, so the joint still closes. Next to an open side the bar ends square.
`x` and `y` are the size of the opening. With `outside` they are the overall size of the frame instead, and the opening is reduced by the bar widths.
All bars are drawn with their front side up and their inner edge at the bottom. The vertical bars are drawn lying down to save material.
Without dove tails the bars only touch each other. Glue them to a backing board or join them with biscuits, dowels or corner brackets.
Created with Boxes.py (https://boxes.hackerspace-bamberg.de/) Command line: boxes Frame Command line short: boxes Frame
